overview: This paper proposes a Bayesian Adversarial Multi-agent Framework for AI-for-Science low-code platforms, which iteratively co-optimizes generated code and test cases through adversarial dynamics and Bayesian prompt updates to enhance the reliability and performance of scientific code generation across diverse base models.

modules.name: Multi-Agent Orchestration System
modules.description: Defines the roles, communication protocols, and interaction topology of the three core agents (Task Manager, Solution Generator, and Evaluator), managing their lifecycle and coordinating the overall execution workflow.

modules.name: Task Planning and Decomposition Module
modules.description: Implements the Task Manager's logic to decompose high-level scientific task descriptions into structured sub-tasks, generate sanity checks, and formulate initial execution plans with interactive user feedback loops.

modules.name: Domain Knowledge Refinement and Injection Module
modules.description: Structures raw user requests, resolves ambiguities, and enriches task descriptions by injecting domain-specific prior knowledge (e.g., physical formulas, data constraints) to bridge the gap between domain experts and code generation.

modules.name: Prompt Construction and Management Module
modules.description: Handles the dynamic assembly of prompts by fusing the user-approved plan, selected test cases, and selected sample code, while maintaining and updating the pools of available test cases and sample codes across iterations.

modules.name: Test Case Generation and Scoring Module
modules.description: Implements the generation of adversarial test cases by the Task Manager and calculates the Test Case Score (S1) to quantify the 'True Hardness' of each test case based on its discriminative capacity for code quality.

modules.name: Solution Generation and Code Scoring Module
modules.description: Executes the Solution Generator agent to produce code candidates based on constructed prompts and calculates the composite Code Score (S2) using the test case execution results and their respective Test Case Scores.

modules.name: Prompt Evaluation and Scoring Module
modules.description: Computes the overall Prompt Score (S3) by aggregating the Code Scores and Test Case Scores to evaluate the effectiveness and likelihood of a specific prompt configuration producing high-quality solutions.

modules.name: Bayesian Optimization for Code Performance Estimation
modules.description: Implements a surrogate model using structural code embeddings (Abstract Syntax Tree) and Gaussian Processes to estimate untested code performance, utilizing an acquisition function to balance exploration and exploitation for candidate selection.

modules.name: Bayesian Recursive Prompt Update Engine
modules.description: Implements the core Bayesian update rule to recursively adjust the probability distribution of selecting test cases and sample codes for subsequent prompts based on the computed prompt scores, driving the co-evolution of code and tests.

modules.name: Adversarial Iterative Refinement Loop Controller
modules.description: Manages the main execution loop that orchestrates the adversarial interaction between the Task Manager (Challenger) and Solution Generator (Solver), applying Bayesian updates and evaluation feedback until a robust solution is found or maximum iterations are reached.

modules.name: Benchmark Evaluation and Metrics Calculation
modules.description: Implements the evaluation logic for general and scientific code generation benchmarks, calculating core metrics such as Pass@k, Valid Execution Rate (VER), Success Rate (SR), and Code-Based Score (CBS).

modules.name: Experiment Runner and Ablation Study Framework
modules.description: Provides the infrastructure to execute full-scale experiments across various base models and benchmarks, including configurations for ablation studies (e.g., with/without Adversarial Test Cases) and robustness tests (with/without expert knowledge).
